title: Illegal Aliens Sentenced For Scheme To Make And Cash Fraudulent Payroll Checks
summary: MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that two foreign nationals unlawfully present in Oklahoma were sentenced on charges relating to a fraudulent payroll check scheme. Bairon Nayn Cabrera-Martinez, 36, an illegal alien from Honduras unlawfully present in LeFlore County, Oklahoma, was sentenced to a term of 33 months in prison for one count of Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud, and 33 months in prison for one count of Unlawful Reentry of Removed Alien. The court set the terms to be served concurrently. On April 1, 2026, Cabrera-Martinez pleaded guilty to the charges in federal district court. Carlos Eduardo Nuila-Ramos, 36, an illegal alien from El Salvador unlawfully present in LeFlore County, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 22 months in prison for one count of Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud and 22 months in prison for one count of Unlawful Reentry of Removed Alien. The court set the terms to be served concurrently. On May 20, 2026, Nuila-Ramos pleaded guilty to the charges in federal district court.
